record.original_question: (T. Breuer, R. M. Guralnick). Let G be a finite simple group and let p1, p2 be any(not necessarily distinct) prime divisors of |G|. Then can we always find Sylow pi-subgroups Hi such that G = ⟨H1, H2 ⟩?

evidence.quote: (T. Breuer, R. M. Guralnick). Let G be a finite simple group and let p1, p2 be any(not necessarily distinct) prime divisors of |G|. Then can we always find Sylow pi-subgroups Hi such that G = ⟨H1, H2 ⟩?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite non-abelian simple group, and let $p_1$ and $p_2$ be any (not necessarily distinct) prime divisors of $|G|$. Does there always exist a Sylow $p_1$-subgroup $H_1$ of $G$ and a Sylow $p_2$-subgroup $H_2$ of $G$ such that 
$$G = \langle H_1, H_2 \rangle?$$
Equivalently, prove or disprove that every finite non-abelian simple group can be generated by two of its Sylow subgroups corresponding to any prescribed pair of prime divisors of its order (allowing the two primes to coincide, in which case $H_1$ and $H_2$ are two Sylow $p$-subgroups for the same prime $p$).
artifact.category_tag: generation of finite simple groups by Sylow subgroups
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Work of Breuer–Guralnick and subsequent results (e.g. Burness–Guest–Harper, "On the generation of simple groups by Sylow subgroups", arXiv:2204.04311) establish that any finite non-abelian simple group can be generated by a Sylow 2-subgroup and a Sylow r-subgroup for any prime r dividing |G|, and more generally by a π-subgroup and a π′-subgroup. The full statement allowing arbitrary, possibly equal, prime pairs (in particular the case p_1 = p_2) does not appear to be fully resolved in the literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: On the generation of simple groups by Sylow subgroups
status_evidence.snippet: If G is a finite nonabelian simple group and r is any prime divisor of |G|, then G is generated by a Sylow 2-subgroup and a Sylow r-subgroup, by combining with work of Breuer and Guralnick.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the case where one of the primes is 2 (for any other prime divisor) is fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Finite groups can be generated by a π-subgroup and a π′-subgroup
status_evidence.snippet: Given a set of primes π, any finite group can be generated by a π-subgroup and a π′-subgroup.
status_evidence.claim: Related Breuer–Guralnick-type generation result for arbitrary finite groups.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook
status_evidence.snippet: Listed among new problems posed by T. Breuer and R. M. Guralnick.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is recorded as an open question in the Kourovka Notebook.
